name: Normokalemic Periodic Paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Normokalemic Periodic Paralysis

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of flaccid muscle weakness without sensory loss
Serum potassium levels remain within normal range during attacks
Electrophysiological evidence of muscle membrane inexcitability during attacks
Positive family history of periodic paralysis or related channelopathies
Exclusion of hypokalemic and hyperkalemic periodic paralysis and other neuromuscular disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent flaccid muscle weakness episodes with normal serum potassium during attacks, electrophysiological confirmation, and exclusion of other periodic paralyses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always definitive due to variable mutations

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal serum potassium levels during paralysis episodes
pathognomonic.notes: Distinguishes from hypo- and hyperkalemic periodic paralysis
searchTerms: no potassium changes with muscle weakness

common.symptomName: Muscle stiffness or cramping preceding weakness
searchTerms: muscle stiffness or cramps before weakness

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness triggered by rest after exercise
Mild myalgia during or between attacks
searchTerms: mild muscle aches during or between attacks
muscle swelling that comes and goes

occasional.symptomName: Dysphagia or dysarthria during severe episodes

occasional.notes: Rare but reported in some cases

searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Normal serum potassium during paralysis episodes
Normal serum calcium and magnesium levels
imaging: Muscle MRI may show mild edema or fatty infiltration in chronic cases
genetic: Mutations in SCN4A gene (voltage-gated sodium channel)
Rare mutations in other ion channel genes
other: Electromyography showing decreased muscle membrane excitability during attacks
Provocative testing with exercise or insulin-glucose may trigger weakness

distinguishingFeatures: More common triggers related to carbohydrate load
Progressive muscle weakness worsened by activity

redFlags: Respiratory muscle involvement causing breathing difficulty
references: Statland JM, Fontaine B, Hanna MG, et al. Review of the diagnosis and treatment of periodic paralysis. Muscle Nerve. 2018;57(4):522-530.
